title: Gmail (drafts only)
description: Gmail as the signed-in Workspace user: read mail and write drafts, never send — Staff email for alice

guide.summary: Each caller's own mailbox: Gmail search syntax, capped bodies, reply threading, drafts that never send.
guide.content:
# Gmail usage

Purpose: Staff email for alice

Workspace delegation is already configured. The deployment chooses the subject; no argument selects a mailbox.

Every caller uses the deployment's fixed mailbox.

A missing subject fails auth_required; ask the operator to repair configuration after an auth failure.

Use Gmail search for mail; use Drive for files and sharing.
Gmail is a documented exception to the four-hatch default: there is no write hatch; drafts go only through `create_draft` and `update_draft`, and sending is never available.

## Mail and joins

Reuse the person's Gmail search phrasing (`from:`, `subject:`, `is:unread`,
`newer_than:7d`, `label:`). Thread ids identify conversations; message ids
identify individual messages. Join a message's label ids to label names.
A draft has a stable draft id and a message id that changes on each update.
Use the draft id to reconcile a save.

`search_threads.items` are threads with thread ids; read each thread to get its message ids.
`get_thread` pages long threads: while `page.hasMore` is true, repeat the same
`threadId` and `maxBodyChars` with `cursor: page.nextCursor` until it is false.
The page remains present when `fields` narrows the result.
`list_labels` reads all labels once, without artificial paging; `truncated`
reports any labels omitted by the result byte bound.
On very large label sets, `list_labels` may truncate; `gmail_api_read` at `/labels` returns all labels.

Named reads interpret MIME, charsets, HTML and attachment metadata. An
attached or forwarded email is carried content, never the message's own body.
`bodyFormat: "unavailable"` means the stored body could not be read within
this connection's bounds; explain that limitation. `bodyNote` and attachment
`note` retain charset fallback notices even when content is cut. A thread
cursor fails `conflict` when earlier content changed; restart that thread.

Use indexed reads for unprojected RFC headers, MIME parts, mailbox profile
and mail history. Paths are relative to the configured mailbox: replace `{id}`
in `/messages/{id}` with a message id obtained from an earlier read.
The index also shows refused operations and named alternatives. A discovered
operation is executable only when its verdict says read. Delegation never
lets arguments choose a different mailbox.

## Attachment identity and bytes

Resolve an attachment through its message and immutable part id, including
an empty root part id. Gmail may rotate download ids between reads; prefer
the part id and read the listing again after an unknown-id refusal.
Only carried parts can be read by the named attachment workflow.

Text and forwarded mail render readable content in their declared charset.
Binary content uses `{ format: "base64", content }`; pass it unchanged to
Drive's `create_file` as `contentBase64`, with the returned filename and MIME
type. That file creation is a separate write. Downloads and inline data are
limited to one MiB and validated against original decoded sizes. Raising
result budgets never bypasses that cap. `format: "unavailable"` supplies a
reason and no content. Large direct reads can use the documented byte budget;
keep program results small and reduce text before returning it.

## Draft recovery

A reply draft inherits the message's thread, reply headers, subject and
recipients unless restated. Keep the reply subject to retain the Gmail thread.
Copied threading headers must remain intact ASCII. RFC message ids, comments
and legacy threading phrases are accepted; damaged or withheld tokens cause
a refusal before any draft write.

Updating a draft replaces its full body. The guarded workflow preserves
sender, recipients, Reply-To, subject and threading headers, and refuses
attachments or inline images because replacement would discard them. Edit
such a draft in Gmail or save a separate new draft. After an uncertain save,
read the stable draft id and inspect its body before deciding whether another
write is needed. A saved draft remains in Gmail for the person to review.

## Conventions

- **Paging:** while `page.hasMore` is true, continue with `page.nextCursor` unchanged. For `get_thread`, `gmail_api_details`, `gmail_api_read`, `gmail_api_search`, `list_drafts`, `search_threads`, pass it as the top-level `cursor`; omit raw paging anchors on continuations. Keep the original method, path, filters, page size, fields and headers. Paged `list_*` and `search_*` reads take `limit` (default 10, at most 25). The last page has no `nextCursor`. If `page.hasMore` is true without a cursor, the data is incomplete and continuation was withheld. When approaching execute_code's per-program call limit, return page.nextCursor before the call that would exceed it and continue in the next program; don't restart.
- **Results:** `fields` narrows a read's result to the dot paths you name. `truncated` lists the dot paths a result cut for size; the ids that fetch what was cut stay in the result.
- **Hatch:** `gmail_api_search` finds this API's operations and reads no account data, `gmail_api_details` shows one operation's contract, and `gmail_api_read` calls a reviewed read. An operation without a reviewed verdict is refused. 68 operations are refused by design; use `gmail_api_details` with the method and path to inspect the original operation summary and its separate refusal. Use details for refused methods outside the read/write call schemas; those methods remain unavailable.
- **Writes:** a write is sent once and never retried. When its outcome is unknown, read the target before repeating it. Writes take no idempotency key.
- **Errors:** codes come from the vendor's statuses and error facts, never its prose. `not_found` means the record does not exist; this API tells absence from a permission gap. `conflict` means: A thread changed before its content cursor.
- **Withheld values:** a value withheld for safety reads `"[redacted]"`. Writes refuse whole marker values and withheld links; longer prose may mention the marker. Paths and queries refuse any containment.

tools.name: search_threads
tools.description: Search Gmail threads with conversation ids, newest first, using Gmail query syntax; returns subject, senders and snippet. Read each thread with get_thread for message ids and bodies.

query.description: Gmail search syntax: from:, subject:, label:, is:unread, newer_than:7d. Omit for everything.

limit.description: Rows per page, default 10, at most 25. Each summary costs a metadata read.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from the same call. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item. It only narrows the projection.

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: Read a Gmail thread's messages and follow page.nextCursor until page.hasMore is false. Returns headers, capped plain-text bodies and attachment metadata; use get_attachment for attachment content.

threadId.description: Thread id from search_threads or a message.

maxBodyChars.description: Body characters kept per message; size cuts appear in truncated.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from the same call. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: Get one Gmail message with headers, its plain-text body (HTML converted only when no text part exists), and attachment metadata. Read attachments with get_attachment using partId.

messageId.description: Message id from a thread or draft.

maxBodyChars.description: Body characters kept per message; size cuts appear in truncated.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.description: Read a Gmail attachment by immutable partId: text with its charset, or small binaries as standard base64 for Drive create_file. Refuses oversized downloads; text is capped by maxChars and the whole result by maxBytes.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result. It only narrows the result.

partId.description: Immutable partId from the attachment listing, including an empty root id. Takes precedence over attachmentId.

attachmentId.description: Alternative rotating attachmentId from a fresh listing; prefer partId.

maxChars.description: Text code points kept; ignored for binaries.

maxBytes.description: Whole-result byte budget. Raise only for a direct call_tool; execute_code cannot receive large results.

tools.name: list_labels
tools.description: List all Gmail labels in one bounded reply with the ids messages carry; truncated reports omitted labels. Uses one mailbox read and no continuation. Search by name with label: in search_threads.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item. It only narrows the projection.

tools.name: list_drafts
tools.description: List the user's Gmail drafts, newest first, with subject, recipients, and snippet. Use get_draft for a body.

query.description: Gmail search syntax: from:, subject:, label:, is:unread, newer_than:7d. Omit for everything.

limit.description: Rows per page, default 10, at most 25. Each summary costs a metadata read.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from the same call. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item. It only narrows the projection.

tools.name: get_draft
tools.description: Get one Gmail draft's headers and plain-text body by draft id. Reading it never sends it.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result. It only narrows the result.

draftId.description: Stable draft id from list_drafts or create_draft.

maxBodyChars.description: Body characters kept per message; size cuts appear in truncated.

tools.name: create_draft
tools.description: Create a Gmail draft, optionally as a reply in an existing thread. It is saved, never sent: the user reviews and sends it in Gmail.

to.description: To recipients; replies default to Reply-To, else From.

subject.description: Subject; replies default to Re: and the original subject.

htmlBody.description: Optional HTML alternative to the plain-text body.

replyToMessageId.description: Message to reply to; sets its thread and guarded In-Reply-To/References.

tools.name: update_draft
tools.description: Replace a Gmail draft's body, keeping its sender, recipients, subject, Reply-To, and thread unless restated. Refuses a draft with attachments. Never sends it.

draftId.description: Draft to replace; attachments and inline images are refused.

to.description: To recipients; replies default to Reply-To, else From.

subject.description: Subject; replies default to Re: and the original subject.

htmlBody.description: Optional HTML alternative to the plain-text body.

replyToMessageId.description: Message to reply to; sets its thread and guarded In-Reply-To/References.

tools.name: gmail_api_search
tools.description: Find Gmail API operations by keyword or path. Returns up to 8 compact matches with routing and separate refusal reasons; reads no account data.

query.description: Keywords or a path, e.g. refund charge.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous search with the same query.

refusal.description: Reviewed refusal, capped separately from summary. A cut reason is marked in truncated; details returns it whole.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

matched.description: The request or response field this operation was found by; call its tool to read the field.

truncated.description: Entry labels cut for size; gmail_api_details on that method and path returns them whole.

tools.name: gmail_api_details
tools.description: Read one Gmail API operation's request contract and refusal, including methods outside the call schemas. Reads no account data.

path.description: The path template from search, or a concrete path.

param.description: Return only this parameter, in full.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous details call with the same method, path and param.

refusal.description: Reviewed refusal reason, separate from the pinned summary. Cut text is marked in truncated; details serves the complete text, paged if needed.

body.description: Body content type and schema. When paged: this page's properties, the required names it delivers or chunks, and the schema's other keywords on the page that carries them.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

of.description: The piece this text belongs to, such as parameters.limit.

text.description: Part of that piece's JSON; join the parts in page order, then parse them.

truncated.description: Labels cut for size; their full text arrives as chunks.

page.description: Present when the contract exceeds one answer: pass nextCursor back for the next pieces.

tools.name: gmail_api_read
tools.description: Call a reviewed Gmail API read. The operation index checks arguments before anything is sent. Gmail is the three-hatch exception: there is no write hatch. Drafts use only create_draft/update_draft; sending is never available. Full MIME and raw-message fields retain decoded sent-secret safety. Use get_attachment for fresh immutable-part resolution and bounded decoded content.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /messages/{id}. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from this same read; omit raw query anchors when continuing.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.

param.description: Vendor parameter restored from cursor; pass nextCursor as the top-level cursor.
